Parsers for model responses

Source: R/parse.R
parsers.Rd

A parser is a function that turns the raw text response of the backend into a single value: a number, a category label, or NA if the response cannot be interpreted. Parse failures are recorded in the run log and reported as part of the validation (a response that cannot be parsed is a failed measurement).

Usage

parse_identity(text)

parse_number(decimal = ".")

parse_choice(levels, aliases = NULL)

parse_json_field(field)

Arguments

text

The raw response text (argument of the returned parser and of parse_identity()).

decimal

Decimal mark for parse_number().

levels

For parse_choice(): the admissible labels, in the order that defines the ordinal scale. Matching is case-insensitive; the longest label occurring in the response wins, so that "likely pathogenic" is not matched as "pathogenic".

aliases

Optional named list mapping additional strings to labels, e.g. list("LP" = "Likely pathogenic").

field

For parse_json_field(): the name of the field to extract from a JSON object in the response (the first {...} block is used).

Value

A function with signature function(text) returning a length-one value.

Examples

parse_number()("The IC50 is approximately 12.5 nM.")
#> [1] 12.5
parse_choice(c("Benign", "Likely benign", "VUS", "Likely pathogenic", "Pathogenic"))(
  "Classification: likely pathogenic (PS1, PM2)")
#> [1] "Likely pathogenic"
parse_json_field("class")('Result: {"class": "VUS", "criteria": ["PM2"]}')
#> [1] "VUS"
